lines: A stereo looper that records a second of audio, plays it back over and over, and lets you speed it up and blend it against the incoming signal

The right channel of the audio to be recorded and mixed against the loop

SH.notes: The signal jacks and the outputs carry whatever is sampled, so no family is set for them. The third section reads A2_PARAM, B2_PARAM, C2_PARAM, D2_PARAM and QU2_PARAM, which are the middle section's controls. The probability test sits inside the `if (!CVcon)` branch only, so it gates generated voltages and not sampled ones; the README says it decides whether an incoming trigger is used at all. The quantise block runs after both branches and so applies to sampled values too, against the README. Per-channel SchmittTrigger arrays are declared and never used; the source carries the comment "NEEDS REPAIR!! Want it to be GTin polyphonic not VoltageSum".

lines: Compares every channel of a polyphonic cable against a threshold and gives gates for above and below, plus the signal itself split the same way
Sets the voltage each channel is compared against, -10V to 10V
Scales the threshold CV before it is added to the threshold knob, 0 to 1
Added to the threshold knob after the attenuator, channel for channel, with the total held between -10V and 10V
The signal to be compared, one channel at a time; its channel count is passed to all four outputs
Carries 10V on each channel whose input is above the threshold, and 0V on the rest
Carries 10V on each channel whose input is at or below the threshold, and 0V on the rest
Carries the input on each channel that is above the threshold, and 0V on the rest
Carries the input on each channel that is at or below the threshold, and 0V on the rest
Note — the comparison is made afresh every sample with no smoothing, so this works at audio rate for hard splitting as well as at modulation rate
Note — the threshold jack is read channel by channel, so a polyphonic cable there gives each channel its own threshold
Note — the two lamps follow the last channel of the cable rather than the whole of it, so with more than one channel patched they do not show the state of the first

lines: Gathers up to sixteen separate cables into one polyphonic cable
One of the cables gathered into the output; its own channels are packed in after those of the jacks above it
Carries every patched input packed into one polyphonic cable, up to sixteen channels in all
Note — the inputs are packed end to end in jack order with no gaps, so unpatched jacks take up no channel; anything past the sixteenth channel is dropped
Note — the lamps show how many channels the output is carrying
Menu — Monophonic Inputs Only — takes only the first channel of each input and places it at that input's own position, rather than packing every channel of every input together
Note — with Monophonic Inputs Only switched on, a gap in the patched jacks puts the channel count out of step with where the voltages are written, so patch from the first jack downwards
Note — the maker's README describes a menu offering a channel count from auto to sixteen; this build's menu has the monophonic switch instead
